name: Willamette Valley

climate: Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris and Chardonnay sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: American Viticultural Area. A wine labeled with one must take at least 85% of its grapes from that area.
Oregon is stricter than federal law: a wine named for an AVA needs 95% of its grapes from that AVA, and one named for an AVA wholly in Oregon must use only Oregon grapes.
keyfacts: Willamette Valley was established as an AVA in 1983.
Predominant soils are marine sedimentary, volcanic and loess.
Northerly latitude and the moderating Pacific Ocean make it one of the coolest winegrowing regions in North America.
Yamhill-Carlton only includes land between ⟦elev|200 and 1,000 feet|61 and 300 m⟧ in elevation.

notes: Oregon Pinot Gris is medium bodied, yellow to copper-pink, with aromas of pear, apple and melon.

blurb.text: Oregon's largest AVA, covering the Willamette River basin, with a cool climate of wet winters and dry summers and worldwide recognition for Pinot Noir. Pinot Noir is 72 percent of plantings, then Pinot Gris. A local Pinot Noir's top-ten finish against Burgundies at the 1979 Gault-Millau Wine Olympics first drew international attention to it.
